question: Who is behind the drone strikes on Zawiya's oil infrastructure?

sideA.label: Zawiya security actors (Bahroun / Isnad Force)
sideA.text: Militia commander Mohamed Bahroun ('Al Far') has labeled the drone campaign against the refinery and grid 'an act of terrorism' directed at Zawiya itself, framing his forces as the target rather than the culprit.

sideB.label: Independent analysts (RUSI)
sideB.text: Analyst Jalel Harchaoui (RUSI) notes the strikes come amid GNU pressure on Bahroun's forces to relinquish control of Zawiya, suggesting the attacks could be tied to the power struggle for the city rather than an external actor.

resolution: No group has claimed responsibility for any of the six strikes (Aug 8–12, 2026) and Libyan authorities have not publicly named a suspect; the case remains unresolved and under investigation.

question: Who assassinated LNA intelligence chief Fawzi al-Mansouri?

sideA.label: GNS/LNA leadership
sideA.text: PM Osama Hamad called it a 'treacherous terrorist act' and pledged a full investigation, implying an organized plot against the LNA's security apparatus.

sideB.label: Independent analysts
sideB.text: Regional analysts note al-Mansouri's close ties to the Haftar family and suggest the killing could stem from internal LNA rivalries as much as external enemies, given the lack of any claim of responsibility.

resolution: Unresolved. No group has claimed the August 10, 2026 car bombing; an LNA investigation is ongoing.

question: Is the June 2026 power-sharing deal a genuine transition or an elite/family capture of the state?

sideA.label: US mediators (Boulos, Rubio)
sideA.text: Massad Boulos says the plan's 'main goal is to unify the Libyans, unify the land, unify the people, and unify the institutions,' and is 'designed to be inclusive, ensuring balanced representation for all stakeholders, regions and cities,' complementing the UN's longer-term electoral roadmap.

sideB.label: Critics (African Arguments, Atlantic Council)
sideB.text: Analysts argue the deal is 'in essence a power-sharing arrangement between the Haftar and Dbeibah families,' elevating Saddam Haftar to a three-person presidency without independent judicial, electoral, or anti-corruption safeguards.

resolution: Contested. The June 18, 2026 trilateral agreement sets an election deadline of February 17, 2027, but implementation of independent institutional guarantees remains unverified as of this update.

question: Who should bear the cost of Libya's fiscal adjustment — the treasury, reserves, or the dinar?

sideA.label: Central Bank of Libya
sideA.text: Governor Naji Issa resigned citing unspecified 'sensitive matters,' widely read as a protest over pressure to keep financing recurrent state spending without corresponding fiscal discipline from the rival legislatures.

sideB.label: HoR / HSC leadership
sideB.text: Both the House of Representatives' Finance Committee and High State Council head Mohamed Takala rejected the resignation, directing Issa to remain in post while a joint reform committee is formed — implicitly resisting further dinar devaluation or reserve drawdowns.

resolution: Unresolved as of August 20, 2026; Issa remains in his post pending the reform committee's recommendations and his own stated conditions for formally withdrawing the resignation.

question: Who bears responsibility for the August 4 Zawiya-Surman clashes?

sideA.label: Mohamed Bahroun (Isnad Force)
sideA.text: Bahroun said, 'We never desired war, nor did we seek confrontation or bloodshed; for the sanctity of life is paramount, and Libyan blood is precious to us all,' framing his forces' actions as self-defense against rival factions.

sideB.label: UNSMIL / local officials
sideB.text: UNSMIL called for those responsible for the clashes to be held accountable, and western municipalities appealed to the Tripoli government for intervention, implying culpability lies with the armed factions regardless of who fired first.

resolution: Contested. At least 8 people were killed; the GNU convened an expanded security meeting and moved to impose calm in Zawiya and Surman, but no formal attribution of blame has been issued.

question: Does the 53% drop in Italy-bound arrivals reflect improved migration control or simply route diversion?

sideA.label: Libyan/Italian authorities
sideA.text: The steep year-on-year decline in central Mediterranean arrivals (11,995 vs 27,303 in H1 2025) is presented as evidence of tightened departure-point enforcement and repatriation efforts, including flights returning migrants via Benina airport.

sideB.label: Migration researchers (Global Initiative, IOM)
sideB.text: Analysts argue the decline mainly reflects diversion to the longer, more dangerous eastern Tobruk–Crete corridor, where crossings surged to roughly 10,000 by early August 2026 from 5,161 in all of 2024 — alongside record Mediterranean-wide deaths and disappearances.

resolution: Both trends are documented: central Mediterranean arrivals are down sharply while the eastern route has grown nearly 2x year-on-year, suggesting displacement of the flow rather than a net reduction in departures.

question: Are Libya's blackouts primarily caused by drone strikes or chronic grid underinvestment?

sideA.label: GNU officials
sideA.text: The government's securing of the Mellitah complex and restoration of gas supply after the July 28 storming suggests officials view immediate sabotage/security threats and militia interference as key drivers of outages.

sideB.label: Al Jazeera investigative reporting / protesters
sideB.text: Coverage of the blackout protests frames the crisis as the product of 'years of underinvestment' in the electricity grid and a 'severe heatwave' driving demand beyond capacity — a structural failure rather than a security event.

resolution: Both factors compound each other: UNSMIL's Hanna Tetteh told the Security Council that outages 'exacerbated by the severe heatwave' exposed 'institutional fragmentation... and governance failures,' while the August 12 substation strike shows attacks add acute, additional damage.

question: Does Saddam Haftar's elevation represent legitimate succession planning or authoritarian dynasty-building?

sideA.label: LNA / Haftar camp
sideA.text: Khalifa Haftar has framed the LNA's modernization under his 'Vision 2030' plan as building 'a sophisticated army capable of facing regional and international challenges,' presenting continuity of command, including his son's role, as institutional strengthening.

sideB.label: Rebel/opposition figures
sideB.text: Rebel leader Mohamed Wardago said 'nobody can accept that Haftar and his sons should hold key sovereign positions within the Libyan state,' while analysts at Foreign Policy and the New Arab argue there is little in the Haftar family's history to suggest genuine power-sharing intent.

resolution: Unresolved; the three-person presidency envisioned by the June 2026 deal has not yet been formally seated as of this update, and opposition to a Haftar-headed executive persists.

question: Has the UAE's tilt toward Turkey-aligned Tripoli abandoned its traditional partnership with Egypt and France on Libya?

sideA.label: Atlantic Council analysis
sideA.text: Analysts describe a 'precarious shift' in UAE policy — choosing not to compromise its rapprochement with Turkey and instead brokering shuttle diplomacy between Dbeibah and Haftar's circles, effectively breaking with long-standing partners Egypt and France.

sideB.label: Egyptian officials
sideB.text: Cairo has pushed back on any Libya-Turkey maritime or defense arrangement, with President Sisi's government pressing Washington to restrain Haftar from endorsing Turkish deals, while also reassessing its own strategy amid concerns over alleged LNA support for Sudan's RSF.

resolution: Contested and evolving; regional alignments around Libya remain fluid as the US-brokered unity process advances.

question: Are the fibre-optic-guided drones used in the Zawiya strikes domestically made or imported?

sideA.label: Local commentary (per Libya Herald reporting)
sideA.text: Some observers argue the fibre-optic drone technology used against Zawiya targets could be homemade, built by local armed groups with access to commercial components.

sideB.label: Alternative theory
sideB.text: Others suggest the drones were imported, pointing to precedents of fibre-optic FPV drone technology transferred from the Ukraine conflict theater into North African and Sahelian militia arsenals.

resolution: Unresolved; Libyan commentators themselves are debating the drones' origin, and no forensic attribution has been publicly confirmed.

question: What did the '4+4' committee actually agree to in the August 20 Tunis election deal?

sideA.label: Public/leaked draft text
sideA.text: Versions of a 'draft final agreement' circulated publicly and in Libyan media shortly after the August 20, 2026 initialling in Tunis, describing specific terms for restructuring the High National Elections Commission and revising electoral laws.

sideB.label: UNSMIL, Presidential Council & High State Council
sideB.text: Two days after the initialling, UNSMIL said the information circulating 'does not accurately reflect what the parties agreed upon.' By August 25, Presidential Council head Mohamed al-Menfi questioned the 'clarity of its basis, its jurisdictions, and its applicability,' and HSC member Nuh al-Malati said the council 'has not yet received an official copy' and that its GNU-linked signatories do not represent its official position.

resolution: Unresolved as of August 25, 2026; beyond UNSMIL's confidentiality dispute, both the Presidential Council and High State Council have now publicly questioned the deal's legitimacy and the signatories' authority to bind their institutions. The authoritative text has still not been published.

question: Was the August 21 Al-Ghiran ammunition depot explosion south of Misrata an accident or an attack?

sideA.label: Initial local reporting
sideA.text: Libyan and wire outlets described a sudden blast triggering cascading secondary explosions of rockets, artillery shells, and tank rounds, consistent with an accidental cook-off at a poorly stored ammunition site.

sideB.label: Unverified alternative
sideB.text: No party has ruled out a deliberate strike or sabotage against the Al-I'sar Battalion, given the same period's unclaimed drone campaign against Zawiya and the unclaimed assassination of LNA intelligence chief Fawzi al-Mansouri.

resolution: Unresolved; authorities had not determined a cause as of the latest reporting, and no casualties were confirmed at local medical facilities.
